Difference in differences after matching on pre-treatment trajectories

Source: R/panel_causal.R
mtchdid.Rd

Matches each treated unit to the comparison units most like it before treatment (its outcomes in the pre-period and, optionally, covariates), within an exact grouping if given, and estimates the difference in differences on the matched sample with the matching weights.

Usage

mtchdid(
  data,
  unit,
  time,
  y,
  ftreat,
  covs = NULL,
  ratio = 1L,
  exact = NULL,
  caliper = NULL,
  covm = c("pooled", "full"),
  conflvl = 0.95,
  cl = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per unit and period.

unit, time, y

Column names: the unit, the period (numeric, for example a year or a month index) and the outcome.

ftreat

Column name of the period a unit is first treated (NA, 0 or Inf for a unit never treated). Treatment is taken as staying on.

covs

Optional covariate columns to match on (their pre-period means).

ratio

Comparison units per treated unit (default 1).

exact

Optional column name: match only within its values (a region, a district).

caliper

Optional maximum distance, in standard deviations of the distances.

covm

"pooled" (default; the pooled within-group covariance) or "full" (the whole sample's).

conflvl

Confidence level of the intervals reported (default 0.95).

cl

Column name of the clusters (default the unit), or two column names for two-way clustering (Cameron, Gelbach and Miller 2011): \(V_a + V_b - V_{ab}\), each term with the small-sample factor of the dimension with fewer clusters, and t on its \(G - 1\) degrees of freedom. A composite cluster (district by month, say) is one column made with interaction(). Fewer than ten clusters give a warning (CR1 errors are unreliable with so few; wcb is made for that case), and so does a cluster that changes within a unit.

Value

A list of class rmbl_matched_did: estimate (a plndid result), matches (treated unit, comparison unit, distance), weights (per unit), balance (a baltab of the matching features before and after).

Details

Each unit is described by its outcome in each pre-period (the periods before the first adoption) and the pre-period means of the covariates. Distances are Mahalanobis, with the pooled within-group covariance of those features (covariance = "pooled", as MatchIt computes it) or their covariance in the whole sample ("full", as stats::mahalanobis() is usually given it); each treated unit takes its ratio nearest comparison units, with replacement (so the matches do not depend on the order of the treated units), only within its exact group, and only within caliper (in units of the distance's standard deviation) if given. A comparison unit's weight is the sum over the treated units it serves of \(1/\code{ratio}\). The estimate is plndid on the matched units with those weights, with errors clustered by unit; matching on pre-period outcomes makes parallel trends more credible but can bring in regression to the mean when the treated were chosen for an unusual pre-period (Daw and Hatfield 2018).

References

Daw JR, Hatfield LA (2018). Matching and regression to the mean in difference-in-differences analysis. Health Services Research 53(6):4138-4156. doi:10.1111/1475-6773.12993

Applied with spatial nearest-facility matching within judicial districts: Zorro Medina A (2020). The failed war on pre-trial detention: evidence from a quasi-experimental reform. doi:10.2139/ssrn.3686855

Examples

p <- polex()
m <- mtchdid(p, "district", "month", "crmrate", "refmonth", ratio = 2)
m$estimate
#> ╭── Difference in differences ────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Method           fixed-effects least squares, cluster-robust (CR1) errors │
#> │   Observations     720                                                      │
#> │   Clusters         20                                                       │
#> │   Confidence       95%                                                      │
#> │   Comparison mean  26.3                                                     │
#> │   Relative effect  -11.7% of the comparison mean                            │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   Estimates                                                                 │
#> │   term     estimate      se  95% CI                 t  p_value              │
#> │   -------  --------  ------  ----------------  ------  -------              │
#> │   treated    -3.081  0.1208  [-3.334, -2.829]  -25.51  < 0.001              │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   The policy's effect on the outcome is -3.081 (95% interval [-3.334,       │
#> │   -2.829]): the interval excludes 0, so the data distinguish it from no     │
#> │   effect.                                                                   │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   The comparison mean is the pre-period mean outcome of the units not       │
#> │   (yet) treated.                                                            │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
m$balance
#>    feature    smdbef  smdafter
#> 1      y_1 0.6234337 0.6305205
#> 2      y_2 0.4933815 0.5333419
#> 3      y_3 0.3630111 0.4016449
#> 4      y_4 0.5185005 0.5671520
#> 5      y_5 0.5394918 0.5670062
#> 6      y_6 0.5953617 0.6497642
#> 7      y_7 0.5296771 0.5555045
#> 8      y_8 0.4786997 0.5442183
#> 9      y_9 0.6411876 0.6298522
#> 10    y_10 0.5844047 0.7157425
#> 11    y_11 0.5414501 0.5442063
#> 12    y_12 0.4630436 0.5330361

# your own panel: eight towns over ten years, four adopting a by-law (two
# in 2019, two in 2021), with each town's population, county and income
own <- data.frame(
  town = rep(c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G", "H"), each = 10),
  year = rep(2015:2024, times = 8)
)
i <- match(own$town, unique(own$town))
own$first <- c(2019, 2019, 2021, 2021, NA, NA, NA, NA)[i]
own$bylaw <- as.integer(!is.na(own$first) & own$year >= own$first)
own$pop <- c(12, 30, 8, 22, 15, 40, 9, 18)[i] * 1000
own$county <- rep(c("North", "South"), 4)[i]
own$income <- 50 + own$year - 2015 + cos(seq_len(80))
own$rate <- 30 + i + 0.5 * (own$year - 2015) - 4 * own$bylaw +
  0.2 * own$income + sin(seq_len(80))
# each adopting town matched to one never treated on its path before 2019,
# the standard errors clustered by county: with two counties the package
# warns that so few clusters cannot be trusted
mtchdid(own, "town", "year", "rate", "first", cl = "county")$estimate
#> Warning: mtchdid: `cl` (county) gives only 2 clusters: cluster-robust (CR1) standard errors are unreliable with so few; wcb() is made for this case

#> │   Observations     60                                                       │
#> │   Clusters         2                                                        │
#> │   Confidence       95%                                                      │
#> │   Comparison mean  46.48                                                    │
#> │   Relative effect  -8.7% of the comparison mean                             │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   Estimates                                                                 │
#> │   term     estimate      se  95% CI                   t  p_value            │
#> │   -------  --------  ------  ------------------  ------  -------            │
#> │   treated    -4.052  0.3065  [-7.9460, -0.1577]  -13.22    0.048            │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   The policy's effect on the outcome is -4.052 (95% interval [-7.9460,      │
#> │   -0.1577]): the interval excludes 0, so the data distinguish it from       │
#> │   no effect.                                                                │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   The comparison mean is the pre-period mean outcome of the units not       │
#> │   (yet) treated.                                                            │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
